title: Manifold Absolute Pressure Circuit Malfunction
problem: The Engine Control Unit (ECU) detects an abnormal signal from the Manifold Absolute Pressure sensor.
symptoms: Reduced engine power; Rough idle; Poor fuel economy
actions: Check MAP sensor wiring for damage; Clean MAP sensor port; Test sensor output, replace if faulty

title: Manifold Absolute Pressure Circuit High Input
problem: The Manifold Absolute Pressure sensor is sending an abnormally high voltage signal to the Engine Control Unit (ECU), indicating high pressure.
symptoms: Engine runs rich; Reduced power; Poor throttle response
actions: Inspect MAP sensor wiring and connector; Test MAP sensor output voltage; Replace MAP sensor if faulty

title: Intake Air Temperature Circuit High Input
problem: The Intake Air Temperature sensor is reporting an abnormally high temperature, indicating an open circuit or faulty sensor.
symptoms: Poor cold starting; High idle RPM; Reduced engine power
actions: Inspect IAT sensor wiring and connector; Test IAT sensor resistance; Replace IAT sensor

title: Engine Coolant Temperature Circuit High Input
problem: The Engine Coolant Temperature sensor is sending an abnormally high voltage signal to the ECU, indicating an open circuit or faulty sensor.
symptoms: Engine overheating warning; Poor cold starting; Incorrect fuel mixture
actions: Inspect ECT sensor wiring; Test sensor resistance; Replace ECT sensor

title: Throttle Position Sensor Circuit High Input
problem: The Throttle Position Sensor (TPS) is sending an abnormally high voltage signal to the ECU, indicating a wide-open throttle or an open circuit.
symptoms: Erratic idle; Poor acceleration; Engine limp mode
actions: Check TPS wiring and connector; Adjust TPS calibration; Replace TPS if faulty

title: O2 Sensor Heater Circuit Malfunction (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
problem: The heater circuit for the primary oxygen sensor is not functioning correctly, preventing the sensor from reaching operating temperature.
symptoms: Increased fuel consumption; Poor emissions; MIL illumination
actions: Check O2 sensor heater wiring; Test heater circuit resistance; Replace O2 sensor

title: O2 Sensor Heater Circuit Malfunction (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
problem: The heater circuit for the secondary oxygen sensor (post-catalyst) is not functioning correctly, affecting catalyst efficiency monitoring.
symptoms: Increased fuel consumption; Emissions test failure; MIL illumination
actions: Check O2 sensor heater wiring; Test heater circuit resistance; Replace O2 sensor

title: System Too Rich (Bank 1)
problem: The Engine Control Unit (ECU) is detecting too much fuel or too little air in the exhaust gas for Bank 1.
symptoms: Poor fuel economy; Black smoke from exhaust; Reduced engine power
actions: Check fuel pressure regulator; Inspect fuel injectors for leakage; Check for restricted air filter

title: System Too Rich (Bank 2)
problem: The Engine Control Unit (ECU) is detecting too much fuel or too little air in the exhaust gas for Bank 2 (if applicable).
symptoms: Poor fuel economy; Black smoke from exhaust; Reduced engine power
actions: Check fuel pressure regulator; Inspect fuel injectors for leakage; Check for restricted air filter

title: Fuel Injector Circuit Malfunction - Cylinder 1
problem: The Engine Control Unit (ECU) has detected an open or short circuit in the electrical circuit of the fuel injector for Cylinder 1.
symptoms: Engine misfire; Rough idle; Loss of power
actions: Check injector wiring for damage; Test injector resistance; Replace injector if faulty

title: Fuel Injector Circuit Malfunction - Cylinder 2
problem: The Engine Control Unit (ECU) has detected an open or short circuit in the electrical circuit of the fuel injector for Cylinder 2.
symptoms: Engine misfire; Rough idle; Loss of power
actions: Check injector wiring for damage; Test injector resistance; Replace injector if faulty

title: Engine Over-speed Condition
problem: The Engine Control Unit (ECU) has detected that the engine RPM has exceeded its maximum safe limit.
symptoms: Engine shutdown; Reduced power; Limp mode activation
actions: Check for faulty RPM sensor; Inspect ECU for internal errors; Avoid exceeding RPM limits

title: Fuel Pump Primary Circuit Malfunction
problem: The Engine Control Unit (ECU) has detected a malfunction in the primary control circuit for the fuel pump.
symptoms: Engine cranks but won't start; Engine stalls; Loss of fuel pressure
actions: Check fuel pump fuse and relay; Inspect wiring to fuel pump; Test fuel pump for operation

title: Random/Multiple Cylinder Misfire Detected
problem: The Engine Control Unit (ECU) has detected misfires occurring in multiple or random cylinders.
symptoms: Rough idle; Loss of power; Engine vibration
actions: Check spark plugs and coils; Inspect fuel injectors; Perform compression test

title: Cylinder 1 Misfire Detected
problem: The Engine Control Unit (ECU) has detected a misfire specifically in Cylinder 1.
symptoms: Rough idle; Loss of power; Engine vibration
actions: Check spark plug and coil for Cylinder 1; Inspect injector for Cylinder 1; Perform compression test on Cylinder 1

title: Cylinder 2 Misfire Detected
problem: The Engine Control Unit (ECU) has detected a misfire specifically in Cylinder 2.
symptoms: Rough idle; Loss of power; Engine vibration
actions: Check spark plug and coil for Cylinder 2; Inspect injector for Cylinder 2; Perform compression test on Cylinder 2

title: Crankshaft Position Sensor 'A' Circuit
problem: The Engine Control Unit (ECU) is not receiving a signal or an incorrect signal from the Crankshaft Position Sensor.
symptoms: Engine cranks but won't start; Engine stalls; Intermittent loss of power
actions: Check CPS wiring and connector; Test CPS resistance; Replace CPS if faulty

title: Camshaft Position Sensor 'A' Circuit
problem: The Engine Control Unit (ECU) is not receiving a signal or an incorrect signal from the Camshaft Position Sensor.
symptoms: Long crank times; Reduced engine power; Poor fuel economy
actions: Check CMS wiring and connector; Test CMS resistance; Replace CMS if faulty

title: Evaporative Emission System Purge Control Valve Circuit Open
problem: The Engine Control Unit (ECU) detects an open circuit in the electrical connection to the EVAP purge control valve.
symptoms: Check engine light; Slight increase in emissions
actions: Check wiring and connector to purge valve; Test purge valve solenoid; Replace purge valve
location: Under fuel tank or near charcoal canister

title: Evaporative Emission System Purge Control Valve Circuit Low
problem: The Engine Control Unit (ECU) detects a low voltage signal or short to ground in the electrical connection to the EVAP purge control valve.
symptoms: Check engine light; Slight increase in emissions
actions: Check wiring for short to ground; Test purge valve solenoid; Replace purge valve
location: Under fuel tank or near charcoal canister

title: Vehicle Speed Sensor Malfunction
problem: The Engine Control Unit (ECU) is not receiving a signal or an incorrect signal from the Vehicle Speed Sensor.
symptoms: Speedometer/odometer erratic or inoperative; ABS/ASC malfunction; Engine limp mode
actions: Check VSS wiring and connector; Clean VSS sensor head; Replace VSS if faulty
location: Transmission output shaft or wheel hub

title: Idle Control System Malfunction
problem: The Engine Control Unit (ECU) is unable to maintain the commanded engine idle speed.
symptoms: Rough or erratic idle; Engine stalls at idle; High idle RPM
actions: Clean IAC valve; Check for vacuum leaks; Test IAC valve operation, replace if faulty

title: System Voltage Low
problem: The Engine Control Unit (ECU) detects that the system voltage is below a specified threshold for a sustained period.
symptoms: Dim lights; Difficulty starting; Electrical component malfunctions
actions: Check battery condition and terminals; Inspect alternator/stator output; Check for parasitic drains

title: System Voltage High
problem: The Engine Control Unit (ECU) detects that the system voltage is above a specified threshold for a sustained period.
symptoms: Bulbs burning out; Overcharging battery; Damage to electrical components
actions: Check voltage regulator; Inspect alternator/stator; Test battery for overcharging

title: Internal Control Module Memory Check Sum Error
problem: An internal error has been detected in the Engine Control Unit's (ECU) memory.
symptoms: Engine won't start; Intermittent engine operation; Multiple DTCs
actions: Check ECU power and ground; Attempt ECU software reflash; Replace ECU

title: Starter Relay Circuit
problem: The Engine Control Unit (ECU) detects a fault in the electrical circuit controlling the starter relay.
symptoms: Engine won't crank; No starter motor engagement
actions: Check starter relay fuse; Test starter relay for continuity; Inspect wiring to starter relay

title: Fuel Pump 'A' Control Circuit/Open
problem: The Engine Control Unit (ECU) has detected an open circuit in the control circuit for the fuel pump.
symptoms: Engine cranks but won't start; Engine stalls; Loss of fuel pressure
actions: Check fuel pump fuse and relay; Inspect wiring to fuel pump; Test fuel pump for operation

title: Malfunction Indicator Lamp (MIL) Control Circuit
problem: The Engine Control Unit (ECU) detects a fault in the electrical circuit that controls the Check Engine Light on the instrument cluster.
symptoms: MIL does not illuminate; MIL stays on constantly
actions: Check MIL bulb/LED; Inspect wiring to instrument cluster; Test instrument cluster for fault

title: Transmission Control System Malfunction
problem: A general fault has been detected within the transmission control system. Specific transmission codes may also be present.
symptoms: Harsh shifting; Transmission limp mode; Inability to shift gears
actions: Check TCU wiring and connectors; Scan for specific transmission sub-codes; Consult BMW diagnostic tool
location: Under seat or fairing, near ECU

title: EWS Control Module Malfunction (BMW Specific)
problem: The Engine Control Unit (ECU) cannot communicate with or authenticate through the Electronic Immobilizer system.
symptoms: Engine cranks but won't start; Key not recognized; Security light flashes
actions: Check EWS module wiring; Try spare key; Reset EWS system with diagnostic tool
location: Under seat or fairing, near ECU

title: Lambda Sensor Signal
problem: The Lambda sensor provides incorrect voltage readings to the ECU, indicating an improper air-fuel mixture.
symptoms: Increased fuel consumption; Poor engine performance; MIL illumination
actions: Check sensor wiring for damage; Verify sensor operation with multimeter; Replace Lambda sensor

title: Lambda Sensor Heater
problem: The heating element within the Lambda sensor is not functioning, preventing it from reaching optimal operating temperature quickly.
symptoms: Increased fuel consumption; Delayed closed-loop operation; MIL illumination
actions: Check sensor heater wiring; Test heater resistance; Replace Lambda sensor

title: Idle Actuator Malfunction
problem: The idle actuator is unable to control the engine's idle speed effectively, possibly due to mechanical or electrical failure.
symptoms: Erratic idle; Engine stalls at idle; High idle RPM
actions: Clean idle actuator; Check wiring and connector; Test actuator operation, replace if faulty

title: Fuel Pump Relay Malfunction
problem: The fuel pump relay is not activating or deactivating the fuel pump as commanded by the ECU.
symptoms: Engine cranks but won't start; Engine stalls; No fuel pump prime sound
actions: Check relay fuse; Test fuel pump relay; Inspect wiring to relay

title: Camshaft Position Sensor
problem: The Camshaft Position Sensor is sending an inconsistent or absent signal to the ECU.
symptoms: Long crank times; Reduced engine power; Poor fuel economy
actions: Check CMS wiring and connector; Test CMS resistance; Replace CMS if faulty

title: Crankshaft Position Sensor
problem: The Crankshaft Position Sensor is sending an inconsistent or absent signal to the ECU, preventing accurate engine timing.
symptoms: Engine cranks but won't start; Engine stalls; Intermittent loss of power
actions: Check CPS wiring and connector; Test CPS resistance; Replace CPS if faulty

title: Throttle Position Sensor
problem: The Throttle Position Sensor (TPS) signal is outside the expected range or is erratic.
symptoms: Erratic idle; Poor acceleration; Engine limp mode
actions: Check TPS wiring and connector; Adjust TPS calibration; Replace TPS if faulty

title: EWS Communication Error
problem: The Engine Control Unit (ECU) is unable to establish communication with the Electronic Immobilizer (EWS) module.
symptoms: Engine cranks but won't start; Key not recognized; Security light flashes
actions: Check EWS module wiring; Verify key programming; Consult BMW diagnostic tool for EWS reset
location: Under seat or fairing, near ECU

title: Front Wheel Speed Sensor
problem: The front wheel speed sensor is sending an incorrect or no signal to the ABS/ASC control unit.
symptoms: ABS/ASC warning light; Speedometer malfunction; Reduced braking efficiency
actions: Check sensor wiring and connector; Clean sensor and tone ring; Replace front wheel speed sensor

title: Rear Wheel Speed Sensor
problem: The rear wheel speed sensor is sending an incorrect or no signal to the ABS/ASC control unit.
symptoms: ABS/ASC warning light; Speedometer malfunction; Reduced braking efficiency
actions: Check sensor wiring and connector; Clean sensor and tone ring; Replace rear wheel speed sensor

title: ABS System Pressure Sensor
problem: The ABS hydraulic unit's internal pressure sensor is reporting an abnormal reading.
symptoms: ABS/ASC warning light; Reduced braking performance; Stiff brake lever/pedal
actions: Check ABS unit wiring; Bleed ABS system; Replace ABS hydraulic unit
location: Under seat or fairing, within ABS unit

title: ABS Pump Motor
problem: The electric pump motor within the ABS hydraulic unit is not functioning correctly.
symptoms: ABS/ASC warning light; No ABS intervention; Spongy brake feel
actions: Check ABS pump motor relay/fuse; Test pump motor power supply; Replace ABS hydraulic unit
location: Under seat or fairing, within ABS unit

title: Ambient Temperature Sensor
problem: The ambient air temperature sensor is sending an implausible or absent signal to the instrument cluster.
symptoms: Incorrect outside temperature display; Possible cold start enrichment issues
actions: Check sensor wiring and connector; Test sensor resistance; Replace ambient temperature sensor

title: Fuel Level Sensor
problem: The fuel level sensor in the fuel tank is providing an inaccurate or no reading to the instrument cluster.
symptoms: Inaccurate fuel gauge; Fuel warning light malfunction
actions: Check sensor wiring and connector; Remove and inspect fuel level sender unit; Replace fuel level sensor

title: Gear Position Sensor Malfunction
problem: The gear position sensor is sending an inconsistent or absent signal to the ECU/instrument cluster.
symptoms: Incorrect gear display; Hard shifting; Engine may stall at idle
actions: Check sensor wiring and connector; Clean sensor; Replace gear position sensor

title: Instrument Cluster Internal Fault
problem: An internal malfunction has been detected within the instrument cluster itself.
symptoms: Gauge malfunction; Warning lights erratic; Display issues
actions: Check cluster power and ground; Attempt firmware update if available; Replace instrument cluster

title: Cruise Control/Brake Switch 'A' Circuit Malfunction
affectedPart: Brake Light Switch / Cruise Control Switch
problem: The Engine Control Unit (ECU) detects a fault in the circuit for the brake light switch, which can affect cruise control.
symptoms: Cruise control inoperative; Brake lights stay on/off; ABS/ASC malfunction
actions: Check brake light switch adjustment; Inspect switch wiring; Replace brake light switch

title: PCM Processor Fault
problem: An internal error has occurred within the main processor of the Engine Control Unit (ECU).
symptoms: Engine won't start; Engine stalls; Intermittent severe performance issues
actions: Check ECU power and ground; Attempt ECU software reflash; Replace ECU

title: A/C Refrigerant Pressure Sensor 'A' Circuit
problem: This code is typically for automotive AC systems. If seen on a motorcycle, it likely indicates a misdiagnosis or an unusual variant of the ECU mapping where a sensor input is misidentified.
symptoms: No specific symptoms for motorcycle
actions: Verify diagnostic tool compatibility; Check for any custom wiring or sensor additions; Ignore if irrelevant

title: Throttle Actuator Control Motor Circuit Open
problem: The Engine Control Unit (ECU) detects an open circuit in the electrical control of the throttle actuator motor.
symptoms: Engine in limp mode; Reduced throttle response; Engine stalls
actions: Check wiring to throttle body; Test actuator motor resistance; Replace throttle body (often integrated)

title: Throttle Actuator Control Motor Performance
problem: The Engine Control Unit (ECU) detects that the throttle actuator motor is not performing as commanded, possibly due to a mechanical issue.
symptoms: Erratic throttle response; Engine in limp mode; Rough idle
actions: Check for mechanical binding in throttle body; Clean throttle body; Replace throttle body (often integrated)
